reason: No proposal concerns JSDoc; shown proposals are about package.json/tsconfig settings, testapp flow wrapping and Schema naming. A rough scan found JSDoc before only about 1108 of 1911 top-level exports in js/ai, core, genkit and plugins src.
No proposal covers Go code; D-5156e2 is about JS testapps only. Go samples register flows and tools with genkit.DefineFlow/DefineStreamingFlow/DefineTool throughout.
No proposal covers Go context passing. Flow and tool functions take ctx context.Context and pass it to Generate/Retrieve calls.

No proposal about context.Background. Most uses are in main or tests, but some appear in library code (ai/tools.go:953, ai/exp/agent.go:1133, ai/exp/sessionstoretest/*, genkit/reflection.go server lifecycle).
No proposal about Go flow I/O types. Struct inputs carry json tags, but many sample flows take or return plain string or other primitive types.
No proposal about NewX vs DefineX. NewTool/NewX constructors are widely used (about 184 call sites), including in tests and dynamic code; I could not determine intent for every site.

No proposal about functional options. Most public APIs take variadic ...Option arguments, but a few take option structs (DownloadRequestMedia(opts *DownloadMediaOptions), ToolContext.Interrupt(opts *InterruptOptions)).
D-5156e2 covers JS defineFlow in js/testapps/agents, not Go. Go uses genkit.DefineFlow, but many flows take string rather than typed structs.
No proposal about genkit.Run. Only basic-flows uses genkit.Run; multi-step flows such as rag simpleQaFlow do not wrap their steps.
No proposal about GenerateData. Structured output uses GenerateData/GenerateDataStream. The only json.Unmarshal uses in samples parse data files, not model output.
No proposal about any/interface{}. Non-test Go code has thousands of uses of any and 61 of interface{}, mostly undocumented.
No proposal about nolint. The only //nolint in go/ (skills.go:1255) has a reason.
No proposal about Go error handling. Code consistently uses explicit if err != nil checks.
No proposal about Go variable naming. Short scopes use short names (ctx, err, i, d, sb).
No proposal about interface placement. Telling where an interface is consumed versus implemented needs package-level analysis that grep cannot settle.
No proposal about comment punctuation. Most comments are full sentences; some fragments lack periods (for example ai/format.go).
No proposal about Go doc comments. About 2437 of 2457 commented funcs start with the function name.
No proposal about TODO format. Only 3 of 27 Go TODOs use the TODO(id): form.
No proposal about GoDoc. About 1188 of 1288 exported funcs in ai, core, genkit, plugins and internal have a preceding doc comment.
No proposal about Example tests. There are 34 Example functions across the ai, genkit, core, tracing and status packages.
No proposal about test mocking. No mocking frameworks are imported; tests define real models and tools with Genkit primitives.
No proposal about default inputs. Sample flows do not declare default input values; DefaultInput appears only in prompt options.
No proposal about sample package comments. The basic-* samples have full explanatory comments; about 12 of 37 sample dirs (menu, ollama-*, modelgarden*, vectorsearch-*) have none.
No proposal about sample references. The only reference found in core or plugin code is a generic samples link in genkit/doc.go.
No proposal about dead code. The Go compiler rejects unused imports; dead code cannot be fully checked without running linters.
No proposal about Go test imports. No _test.go file imports stretchr/testify.
No proposal about Go assertions. Plain if blocks with t.Errorf are used throughout, and about 3576 of 6821 Errorf/Fatalf messages use the want form; others say 'expected' or report a bare error.
No proposal about cmp.Diff. cmp.Diff appears in 33 test files and reflect.DeepEqual in 34 (108 uses).
No proposal about Go idioms. 95 files import slices and 33 import maps; about 10 sort.Slice/sort.Strings uses remain.
No proposal about flow testing. Tests call .Run(ctx, ...) directly (about 168 occurrences).
No proposal about schema assertions. InputSchema/OutputSchema assertions appear in 29 test files; not every DefineX test checks them.
No proposal about mock models. Core tests define fake/echo models; a few plugin live tests call real APIs.
No proposal about Go logging. core/logger is used about 161 times, but direct slog calls remain (about 102), including slog.InfoContext(ctx, ...) in plugins/googlecloud where a ctx exists.
No proposal about log message style. Most messages are lowercase with key/value attributes; about 40 start with a capital and some end with a period (firebase telemetry).
No proposal about Sprintf in logs. 5 log calls in plugins/googlecloud build the message with fmt.Sprintf.
No proposal about log attribute keys. No log call uses "err"; 99 use "error".
No proposal about log levels. Info is mostly used for lifecycle events, while googlecloud telemetry logs per-request data at Info.
No proposal about log-and-return. One instance found: genkit/servers.go:308 logs the context-provider error and returns it.
No proposal about license headers. All 576 .go files carry the Google LLC header, but 151 lack the SPDX line and 29 lack the Apache text.
No proposal about CLI command names. Most are noun:verb (flow:run, trace:get, eval:run); exceptions include start:flutter, init:ai-tools and dev:test-model.
No proposal about CLI argument names. Arguments are camelCase (<flowName>, <traceId>, <inputFileName>, [modelOrCmd]).
No proposal about MCP tool names. All registered tools are snake_case verb_noun (list_flows, run_flow, start_runtime, get_trace, list_genkit_docs).
No proposal about CLI layout. All commands live in src/commands and use commander's Command.
No proposal about runWithManager. Eight runtime commands use it; start and dev:test-model manage the manager directly.
No proposal about CLI logging. The tools-common logger is used, but trace-list, log-list, trace-get and flow-run use console.log (27 calls), mostly to print data output.
No proposal about JSON/file output. trace:get, log:list and the flow/eval commands offer --format json/jsonl or --output; trace:list showed no such option.
No proposal about --stream. flow:run, the streaming-capable command, provides -s/--stream.
No proposal about MCP tool registration. defineInitPrompt(server) fits the rule; the static defineDocsTool also takes an optional projectRoot.
No proposal about MCP runtime tools. defineFlowTools, defineRuntimeTools and defineTraceTools take (server, options: McpToolOptions) and use options.manager.
No proposal about getCommonSchema. Runtime tools build inputSchema with getCommonSchema(options.explicitProjectRoot, ...).
No proposal about resolveProjectRoot. Runtime handlers call it and return the result when it is not a string.
No proposal about MCP error results. Handlers catch errors and return isError: true with 'Error: ...' text.
